current_example.title: Example: Evaluating Special Values of Logarithms

q-26049.name: Question 1
q-26049.worked_solution:
The logarithm reverses the action of the exponent. The principle is:

$$
{log}_{b}⁡({b}^{x})=x
$$

In our case, we have $b=7$ and $x=\frac{2}{5}.$ Therefore:

$$
{log}_{7}⁡({7}^{2/5})=\frac{2}{5}.
$$

q-26049.html:
Question 1
?

Calculate log7⁡(72/5) without using a calculator.

a
5
b
52
c
15
d
7
e
25
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The logarithm reverses the action of the exponent. The principle is:

logb⁡(bx)=x

In our case, we have b=7 and x=25. Therefore:

log7⁡(72/5)=25.

q-108074.name: Question 4
q-108074.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite $256$ as a power of $2$ (the base of the logarithm) as follows:

$$
256={2}^{8}
$$

Therefore, we have:

$$
{log}_{2}⁡256={log}_{2}⁡({2}^{8})
$$

The logarithm reverses the action of the exponent. The principle is:

$$
{log}_{b}⁡({b}^{x})=x
$$

In our case, we have $b=2$ and $x=8.$ Therefore:

$$
{log}_{2}⁡({2}^{8})=8
$$

logb⁡(bx)=x

q-26042.name: Question 6
q-26042.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite $\frac{1}{81}$ as a power of $3$ (the base of the logarithm) as follows:

$$
\frac{1}{81}=\frac{1}{{3}^{4}}={3}^{-4}
$$

Therefore, we have:

$$
{log}_{3}⁡(\frac{1}{81})={log}_{3}⁡({3}^{-4})
$$

The logarithm reverses the action of the exponent. The principle is:

$$
{log}_{b}⁡({b}^{x})=x
$$

In our case, we have $b=3$ and $x=-4.$ Therefore:

$$

$$

Therefore, we have:

$$
{log}_{3}⁡(\frac{1}{27})={log}_{3}⁡({3}^{-3})
$$

The logarithm reverses the action of the exponent. The principle is:

$$
{log}_{b}⁡({b}^{x})=x
$$

In our case, we have $b=3$ and $x=-3.$ Therefore:

$$
{log}_{3}⁡({3}^{-3})=-3
$$
